t: You're looking at a statue of Captain Robert Falcon Scott, the naval officer and explorer who led two Antarctic expeditions, the Discovery Expedition from 1901 to 1904 and the Terra Nova Expedition from 1910 to 1913. It stands on Waterloo Place and is Grade II listed. What makes it special is the sculptor: Kathleen Scott, his wife. She trained in London and Paris, and made several public monuments, including statues of her first husband. So this is a portrait of an explorer, made by someone who knew him.
